question: A trauma patient who is tachycardic and oliguric but has a systolic blood pressure of 110 mmHg is haemodynamically stable and does not require urgent fluid resuscitation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. In compensated (Class II) haemorrhagic shock, catecholamine-driven vasoconstriction can maintain blood pressure while heart rate and urine output reveal tissue hypoperfusion. Do not be reassured by a normal systolic pressure in isolation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Tachycardia and oliguria are signs of compensated shock; the 'normal' blood pressure is maintained by intense sympathetic vasoconstriction. These patients need urgent resuscitation.
